source_scope: 59 selected source, target configuration, protocol rule and build inputs match the Linux workspace byte-for-byte; not a hermetic whole-worktree release manifest.

execution.runtime: root native host product CLI and product BPF, real isolated Net-SNMP/chrony/coturn containers
execution.build_location: remote Linux unprivileged temporary Docker build

findings.change: Add repeatable formal-CLI acceptance for all eight existing entries. Share lifecycle and bounded byte checks with DNS, while keeping protocol-specific client expectations and target safety. Add phase-oracle negative checks.
notes: SNMP response stages remain generic candidates, not correlated success; noSuchObject is an independently checked exception.
Unsynchronised NTP packets are retained and accepted as responses, but do not satisfy sync time-reply phases.
Short NTP/STUN datagrams remain captured bytes but do not satisfy full request phases.
STUN success and 420 error response phase/socket sets remain separate.

validation.clippy_command: cargo --config profile.dev.package.gewyvern.opt-level=2 clippy --locked --lib --bin gewyvern_validate --test native_validation_harness_tdd -- -D warnings

limits: Small direct IPv4 UDP messages on one host/kernel. IPv6 DNS is a regression, not IPv6 SNMP/NTP/STUN proof.
The product selects cgroup and UDP port. Excluded neighbor sockets were created before entering the selected cgroup, not removed through a per-socket product allowlist.
Complete packet-byte multiset equality is bounded to captured payloads of at most 128 bytes. No per-transaction ordering or cross-window correlation claim.
Native client SNMP ID, NTP origin and STUN transaction/address checks are independent oracles, not claimed product correlation features.
No SNMPv3, SET/traps/informs, full MIB walk, accurate or disciplined host time, NTS, TURN/NAT/ICE or authentication proof.
No sustained-load, performance, vulnerability-classification or process-attribution proof. Trust remains unverified-local.
No release artifact, protocol-count or status-maturity promotion. Existing protocol entries are exercised through the formal product collector.
